sections.title: What's new
items: Unavailable songs

A song Roon can no longer play, because its file is gone or the streaming service dropped it, now says "Unavailable" in red as it does in Roon, and its row is dimmed. This shows in playlists, the queue, album pages and an artist's Tracks. Clicking such a song does nothing. In a playlist the X still takes it out.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Hearts missing from the Tracks page

A song hearted on an album page, in a playlist or from the player didn't show up under the Tracks page's hearts filter until the library was read again, and a song newly added to your library didn't show on the Tracks page at all until then. The same went for taking a heart off. Wrapped's copy of your library now hears of every heart and every added song as it happens.
Hearts missing in playlists
In a playlist, a hearted song from Qobuz or TIDAL showed an empty heart. Playlists now read each song's heart from your library.
Playlist songs that aren't in your library
In a playlist, a song that isn't in your library showed a heart that did nothing when clicked. It now shows a +, which adds the song to your library, as on an album page.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Deep Dive lists that didn't save

In 1.6.0 a Deep Dive could go all the way through and then fail to save, with "unknown track handle". The Hearts & Library link's reconnect (the one that gives memory back after a lot has been read) could happen in the middle of making the list. It now waits until a Deep Dive, Discover or Home list is finished, and two minutes more.

sections.title: What's new
items: Deep Dive in the background

While a Deep Dive is being made, the cover that says what it's working on stays on the Deep Dive page only. Every other page of Wrapped can be used meanwhile, with the progress shown in small text at the bottom right, where a library scan shows its own.

sections.title: What's new
items: Media Keys

Your keyboard's Play/Pause, Stop, Next and Previous keys now control the zone selected in Toasted, in any app. This is on by default, so while Roon is connected other apps (Spotify, YouTube and so on) no longer get those keys. Turn it off in Settings > Hotkeys & Media Keys > Media Keys > Playback. A second switch, Volume, is off by default: on, the Volume Up, Volume Down and Mute keys change the zone's volume instead of the Windows volume, and holding a key keeps going.
Roon profiles

Toasted now knows about your Roon profiles. Pick one from the profile button next to the Wrapper's title, or at the top of either Settings list. Hearts, bans, listening history, Last.fm, Home, Discover and Deep Dive are kept per profile; the library and the playlists are shared, as in Roon. Picking a profile here doesn't change the one Roon's own app is on.
A page for each profile

The wrench next to the profile opens its page in Wrapped's Settings: its Last.fm username (Roon's, or one you type), whether it gets Discover lists (on for the account's first profile), Rescan daily with a Rescan button, and a choice between the shared General settings and settings of its own.
Bans

A Ban button for the player (off by default: Hearts & Library, Ban button) bans the song that's playing for the profile in use. Artist pages have a ban button of their own, and albums can be banned too. Bans are Roon's own, so Roon skips them as well, and nothing banned is picked by Discover, Home or Deep Dive. History has a Banned button with the banned songs, albums and artists, where a ban can be lifted.
Settings in pages

Toasted's Settings and Wrapped's Settings are now a list of pages down the left side, one page at a time, instead of one long scroll. The Roon Core page's entry has a light that shows the connection, and each card's help folds out at its bottom.
Add to playlist
A new button left of Previous adds the playing song to a playlist: pick one, or type a name for a new one. Every song's menu has Add to Playlist too, and an album page's button adds the whole album.
Delete playlists
Playlists can be deleted from Wrapped, with the bin on the Playlists page or on the playlist's own page.
Tracks on artist pages

Artist pages have a Tracks section over the albums. Popular is the artist's songs in Last.fm's top-songs order, and My Library is their songs in your library, the ones you've played most first. The cover plays the song, and More shows up to 30.
Artist banners
Artist pages show Roon's wide photo of the artist, with their picture square at its left, and the name, tags and buttons over it.
Genres and tags in Now Playing
The Wrapped piece in Now Playing can show the playing song's genres and its Roon tags (two checkboxes in the layout editor, and one for their titles). Click one to open its page.
Now Playing links
A new setting in Wrapped's Settings, General: the album and artist links in Now Playing can open Wrapped's own pages instead of Roon's.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Memory use

After reading the library, Toasted held on to a lot of memory, hundreds of megabytes and well over 2 GB with a large library, and the amount could grow each day it stayed open. It's now given back a couple of minutes after the read.
Crash reports
A crash where Windows itself stops Toasted (a memory fault) left nothing in the log. It now leaves a line saying what happened and a snapshot (crash-*.dmp), like Toasted's other crashes.
Hearts with several profiles
With more than one Roon profile, a heart could land on the wrong profile. Hearts now go to the profile picked in Toasted.
Now Playing links on another zone

When Roon's own window was on a different zone than the player, clicking the album or artist in Now Playing opened the wrong page. The link is now checked first, and Roon's search finds the right page when it doesn't match.
Artists that share a name
An artist could get the tags of another band with the same name (Roon's 11th Hour got a rapcore band's). Opening the artist's page now checks the tags against where Roon says the artist is from.
Open in Roon
On some artist pages Open in Roon waited four seconds before showing Roon's page. It now shows it as soon as the page is ready.
Last.fm errors
A passing Last.fm error no longer stops a scrobble read; it's tried again.

sections.title: Good to know
items: One more read
After updating, Wrapped reads the library once more by itself so hearts and bans are right for every profile.
Profiles start empty
A profile other than your first has its own history, Home and Deep Dives, so it starts with only what that profile has played. What you had before stays with the first profile.
A short reconnect after a library read

To give that memory back, the Hearts & Library link reconnects a couple of minutes after Wrapped reads the library (a Rescan, or the daily one). It takes about three seconds. A heart, ban or add to library clicked in the player meanwhile is held and goes through once the link is back; a Wrapped album or artist page that was open may need reopening.
Memory in the log
The log now notes how much memory Toasted uses, and how much of it the Hearts & Library link holds, whenever that changes much.
Return Roon
The Return Roon button moved to the right side of the Wrapper's title bar, next to Settings.
Popular needs a Last.fm key
Without a Last.fm key (Wrapped's Settings), the Popular tab shows the songs in Roon's own order.

sections.title: What's new
items: A log for problems

Toasted now keeps a log, toasted-log.txt in its app data folder (%APPDATA%\com.vulkan.roon-toasted). It notes what Toasted does as it starts and connects, and any errors. It stays small and never leaves your PC.
Crash reports
If Toasted crashes, the log notes where and why, and a snapshot of that moment is saved next to it (crash-*.dmp) before Toasted closes.
Freeze reports

If Toasted ever stops responding, it notes in the log what it was doing and saves a snapshot of the moment (hang-*.dmp, next to the log) that shows exactly where it got stuck. If Toasted freezes on you, attaching both to a GitHub issue helps get it fixed, and the same goes for crashes.

sections.title: What's new
items: List view

Albums, Artists and Genres can show as a list as well as a grid: the grid and list switch sits at the top right of each page. The grid's cards come in three sizes, S, M and L. Each page remembers its own choice.
Sort by column
In the list, click a column's heading to sort by it, and click it again to reverse it, like on Tracks. In the grid, the By tabs sort the same way. Each page remembers its sort.
Record labels and start years
Albums show their record label, and Artists show the label of their newest album and the year they started (from Roon, or from MusicBrainz through Wrapped's tagging). The filters find labels too.
Tracks columns

Tracks has a Columns button with a switch for every column. New columns: Track number, Album artist, Composer, Format, Dynamic range, Plays, Last played and File name. Every column sorts from its heading.
Rearrange columns
Turn on the wrench, then drag a heading onto another to move its column there. Reset order puts them back. It works on Tracks, and on Albums, Artists and Genres in list view.
New Genres page

Genres are tiles sized by how much of your library they hold, biggest first, with their pictures tinted in your accent color. The top half of a tile opens its sub-genres in a panel under it, and theirs inside that, as deep as they go; the bottom half opens the genre. In list view the genre's name opens its sub-genres under it and the rest of the row opens the genre. Genres with nothing of yours in them are left out.
Roon's genres or Wrapped's
A new Genres card in Wrapped's Settings picks whose genres the Genres page shows: Wrapped's own (from the tags it keeps for your artists) or Roon's, with Roon's pictures and sub-genres.
Sub-genres for Wrapped's tags

Wrapped's genres now nest: melodic death metal sits under death metal, metalcore and grindcore under metal, darksynth under synthwave, and so on. A genre's counts and its page take in its sub-genres' artists.
Genre pages show your library
A genre's page now opens to the artists and albums in your library, in grid or list, with a filter and sorting. Roon's top and recommended picks for it are on their own tab.
Artist pictures like Roon's

Artists show the same pictures as Roon, logos included, and hundreds of pictures that didn't load before now do. For artists Roon has no picture of, Wrapped looks on Deezer and uses its picture when that artist has one of your albums or songs.
Roon's artist order
Artists sort the way Roon sorts them, so "The Beatles" is under B and ":wumpscut:" under W.
Heart column
On Tracks the heart is its own column: it sorts by hearted, moves like the others, and can be switched off in Columns.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Taskbar and Alt+Tab
The taskbar widget, the toasts and the Enable Wrapper button no longer show up in the taskbar or in Alt+Tab.
Enable Wrapper
The button sits next to the minimize button in Roon's title bar, out of the way of the title.
Library shuffle
A library shuffle on the Tracks page carries on after Toasted restarts, as long as its songs are still in the zone's queue.

sections.title: Good to know
items: Read the library once
Labels, start years and the new Tracks columns fill in after one more Read the library, in Wrapped's Settings.
Plays
Plays and Last played come from your Last.fm history.
Artists refresh
Each time Toasted connects to Roon it reads your artists again (a few seconds), so their pictures and order stay current.
Deezer pictures
Each artist is looked up on Deezer once; a found picture is kept, and one not found is looked for again after 30 days.

sections.title: What's new
items: Custom colors

Colors has a third choice, Custom, in Toasted's Settings and in Wrapped's Settings. Pick your own accent with the color picker or paste a hex code. The background follows its hue, or pick a background color of your own. The Toaster, the widget, the toasts, Wrapped and Settings all use it.
Custom backgrounds

Now Playing's Background has a Custom choice: a solid color, a gradient (vertical, horizontal, diagonal, reverse diagonal or radial), or an image from your PC. Show the image as Fill, Center or Stretch, or place it yourself: drag it, resize it by its edges and corners, and hold Alt to keep its shape. Blur softens it, and your color shows wherever it doesn't reach. The images you've picked stay in a list to choose from again.
Tint
Gives the album art, or your image, a touch of your accent color.
Blur edge
The album art carries on past its edges, mirrored, then softens and fades away. You choose how far it reaches.
Opacity
Every piece of Now Playing has an Opacity slider, for one piece or all of them at once.
Tertiary color
Invert colors is now Tertiary color: Standard, Invert, or Custom, with your own two colors in place of white and the accent.
Skip Stuck Songs
Roon sometimes stops at the end of a song and never starts the next one. Toasted now moves on to it after a few seconds stuck there. It's on by default, under General in Toasted's Settings.
Settings
Every switch in Toasted's Settings is now a pair of buttons, with the On side in your accent color.
Edit layout
Keep shape and Fit to this window moved up next to Show, and the toolbar's groups move to lines of their own in a narrow window. A bar's custom color uses the new color picker.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Edit layout
The toolbar stays on top when you select a piece. Selecting the album art used to cover it.
Color pickers
Escape closes just the picker, not the editor behind it.

sections.title: Good to know
items: Saved per profile
Custom backgrounds, Tint, Blur edge, Opacity and Tertiary color are saved with each Now Playing profile.
Roon ARC
Skip Stuck Songs works on your Roon zones. Roon ARC's playback isn't shared with apps like Toasted, so it can't help there.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Weekly lists

Discover Weekly and Library Rediscover now make themselves every Monday, as promised. They only ever built when you pressed Build now. If your PC is off on Monday, they're made the next time Toasted runs.

sections.title: Good to know
items: Your first lists
A list you've never had is made the next time Toasted starts, not right away, so a tier or the Last.fm key you set up in the meantime is in it from the start. Build now still makes one any time.

sections.title: What's new
items: Wrapped

The Wrapper gets pages of its own. The Wrapped button over Roon's logo, and its side menu, open Home, Discover, Deep Dive, Radio, History and Settings, plus your library: Genres, Artists, Albums, Tracks, Playlists, Listen Later and Tags. Album and artist pages bring similar artists, tags and play menus. Wrapped runs on the Hearts & Library link.
Home

Your Wrapped playlists, your week, artists for you, new albums from the artists you listen to and from ones you may like, newer albums you may have missed, forgotten favorites, and what you played on this day in earlier years.
Discover

Discover Weekly (artists you've never played, one song each) and Library Rediscover (favorites you haven't played in a year or more), made every Monday and saved in Roon. Rate a song with the thumbs in the player, and Fine Tuning takes requests in your own words.
Deep Dive
Playlists made to order from the songs, albums or artists you pick and what you ask for. Smart Radio needs nothing but the picks.
Tiers

Discovery gets smarter with each tier you set up in Settings: tier 1 reads Last.fm tags (a free key), tier 2 a language model (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, or Ollama on your own PC), tier 3 listens to the songs. Lights on Discover and Deep Dive show what each tier has.
History
Everything you've played in Roon, plus your Last.fm scrobbles from before, with your top artists, albums and tracks for any stretch of time.
Now Playing
One Style list for the bars with new waveform looks (Peak caps, Pixel, Stitch, Line graph, Contour), Loudness coloring, and a Wrapped menu with Discover, Deep Dive, the artist and the album.
Player bar
Discover and Deep Dive sit left of the controls, radio on the left and shuffle and repeat on the right, and the heart right after the song's name.
Onboarding
A short walkthrough the first time you open each part of Wrapped. Replay it or switch it off in Settings.
Settings
Default Menu (Wrapped's side menu and Home, or Roon's own, when Wrapped opens), Live albums (off by default: left out of everything Wrapped picks), page size and colors.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Play on a returning zone
Play works on a zone Roon brings back stopped, even when Roon says play isn't allowed.
Sidebar colors
Roon's sidebar keeps Toasted's colors while you resize or drag the Wrapper.
Folded sidebar
A Wrapped page that's open when Roon folds its sidebar away now takes the freed space.

sections.title: Good to know
items: Not an official API
Wrapped uses a part of Roon that isn't open to apps, like the hearts, so a Roon update can stop it for a while.
Optional tiers
Tiers 2 and 3 are optional. Tier 2 with an online service uses your own key, and the names of songs and artists go to that service.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Wrapper freezing
Resizing the Wrapper could lock it up (Not Responding, tray menu dead, force close needed). Two parts of Toasted were waiting on each other; they no longer can.
Wrapper too small
The Wrapper could be made shorter than Roon's own minimum, leaving Roon hanging out below the player bar. It now stops at a size that fits Roon.
Play greyed out
After a PC restart the zone could show as not ready (play greyed out, Fixed volume, 0:00) until Roon's next change. Zone updates from Roon that carry several changes at once are now read in full.

sections.title: Good to know
items: Narrower Wrapper

The Wrapper can go down to about 760 px wide now (Roon folds its sidebar away below about 1400, the hamburger button brings it back). The player bar's seek and volume bars shorten to fit; text, icons and art stay the same.

sections.title: What's new
items: Roon: Wrapped (experimental)

The Roon app inside a Toasted window, with Toasted's player along the bottom, so everything Roon can do is right there. Switch it on in Settings > The Wrapper, then open it from the tray (double-click opens it while it's on), its hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+W) or Settings. Closing it keeps Roon running out of sight, so it reopens instantly.
Return Roon
Gives Roon its own window back. An Enable Wrapper button then sits in Roon's title bar to wrap it up again.
Now Playing
Click the album art in the player bar for a full-window player. Hit the pencil to move and resize the art, track info, controls, seek bar, zone, quality light and volume anywhere you like.
Make it yours

Fonts per piece (bundled or any installed font), icon packs (Lucide, Phosphor, Tabler, Material Symbols, Remix), a plain or circled play button, and bar styles for seek and volume: Line, Thick, Hairline, Segments, Wave, Spectrum, Beam, Glow line, LED meter, Ribbon, Neon tube, Mountains, Particles, Plasma and Album art. Bars can take the app's colors, the album's, or your own. The player bar can follow the same style. With Hearts & Library on, the seek bar can show a local file's real waveform from Roon instead (Waveform: Roon, Pills, Solid shape, Neon outline, LED or Album art, optionally Alive (bouncing gently near the playhead) and colored by loudness), falling back to the bar style when Roon has none.
Profiles
Save your layouts as profiles and switch between them. Start from the Default, Waves or Waves Large presets.
Toaster on or off
Only want the Wrapper? Switch the Toaster off in Settings > Toaster, or from the tray. Its hotkeys, links, and toast and widget clicks then open the Wrapper instead.
Audio quality

With Hearts & Library on, a small light shows what's playing as Roon receives it: Low Quality, CD Quality or Hi-Res. Hover it for the name. It sits by the zone in the Wrapper's player bar and the Toaster, and is a piece of its own in Now Playing, where it can also show the file's format next to it (like FLAC 96kHz 24bit 2ch).
Search in Roon
With the Wrapper on, the Search hotkey and Stream Deck search can open Roon's own search instead of the Toaster's. Pick Roon or Toaster next to the Search hotkey in Settings > General.
New look
A new Toasted icon in the tray, the taskbar and every title bar, and a Roon: Wrapped logo of its own for the Wrapper.
Changelog
This window. It opens after each update, and the Changelog button in Settings > Updates brings it back. New settings glow until you hover over them.

sections.title: Good to know
items: Tray
The tray menu has Toaster, Wrapper and Taskbar Widget switches. While the Wrapper is on, Open Wrapper comes first and a double-click opens it.
Remember Player
Settings > The Wrapper: Now Playing comes back as you left it, open or closed, even after a restart. Something Roon itself doesn't do.
Open at Launch
Settings > The Wrapper and Settings > Toaster: open either one whenever Toasted starts, at sign-in or by hand. On for the Wrapper to begin with.
Wrapper size
The Wrapper opens where and at the size you left it (maximized excepted).
Main artist only

Some tracks list a long line of supporting artists. Settings > General > Artists: Main shows just the first one Roon lists, in the Toaster, the Wrapper, toasts, the widget and the queue. On to begin with; All brings the full list back.
Settings

A new General card holds what applies to the whole app: Colors, Auto-Hide, Start with Windows and every hotkey. The Hotkeys switch sits on the Hotkeys heading, and the Toaster, Wrapper and Taskbar Widget switches sit next to their titles.
Updates
Toasted now looks for an update 10 seconds after it starts (it was a minute), and again when you open Settings if the last look is over 10 minutes old.

sections.title: Fixes
items: Finding your Core

On PCs with virtual or VPN network adapters (WSL, Docker, Hyper-V, Tailscale), Toasted could miss the Core until a reboot. It now searches on every network adapter and asks the Core's last known address directly.

sections.title: What's new
items: Manual Core address
Settings > Roon Core > Manual: type your Core's IP (and port, if you changed it in Roon) for networks where the search can't get through.
Search and Diagnostics
Search looks for Cores again right away. Diagnostics shows what the search sees, with a Copy button for bug reports.

sections.title: What's new
items: Hearts & Library (experimental)
Heart the playing track, or add it (or its whole album) to your library, right from the Playing tab.
Album pages
Albums by the playing artist open in the Toaster, and artist pages split Albums from Singles & EPs.
Automatic updates
Toasted checks for new versions and installs them with one click.
Settings
Tidied up.

sections.title: First release
items: Roon: Toasted
A Roon companion for Windows: now playing, queue, browse and search, now-playing toasts, global hotkeys and a taskbar widget.
